CHALLENGE C0039 | Evidence: The finding is factually incorrect. In Python's regex engine, the non-greedy `(.+?)` matched before an optional group `(?:\s+\[(.+?)\])?` at the end of the string (`$`) will evaluate shorter matches first. When a shorter match allows the optional group to match before `$`, the engine accepts it and captures the error code successfully. Example: `re.match(r"^(.+?):\s+(.+?)(?:\s+\[(.+?)\])?$", "f: error  [code]").groups()` yields `('f', 'error', 'code')`. The regex does not fail.
